Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search
entries.description:
Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    jql: JQL query string.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return.
    limit: Maximum number of results.
    start_at: Starting index for pagination.
    projects_filter: Comma-separated list of project keys to filter by.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    page_token: Pagination token from a previous search result (Cloud only).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the search results including pagination info.

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

projects_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of project keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER if provided.

page_token.description: (Optional) Pagination token from a previous search result. Cloud only — Server/DC uses start_at for pagination.

input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (Salesforce PWA Kit v3 on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10; customisations under `overrides/`, base package under `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`).

I am auditing an effort estimate for SFCC-804: "Marketing Opt-In Capture for Apple Pay & Google Pay Express Checkout Customers". The ask is to capture marketing opt-in consent from shoppers who check out via Apple Pay / Google Pay express checkout (which normally skips the page where the opt-in checkbox lives). Jira note says "Under shipping and on top of payments."

The CRITICAL question: **is Apple Pay / Google Pay express checkout even implemented in this codebase yet?** If not, SFCC-804 depends on unbuilt work and that is a sequencing finding.

Investigate READ-ONLY (modify nothing) and report with absolute file paths + exact snippets:

1. **Express payments / wallet buttons.** Grep case-insensitively across `overrides/` AND `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` for: `applepay`, `apple pay`, `apple-pay`, `googlepay`, `google pay`, `google-pay`, `express`, `expresscheckout`, `walletbutton`, `paywithgoogle`. Distinguish clearly between (a) real Zimmermann implementation in `overrides/`, (b) base SFCC template code, (c) incidental matches inside vendor SDK type definitions. State plainly whether an express-checkout wallet flow EXISTS, is PARTIAL, or is ABSENT.

2. **Adyen.** Grep `overrides/`, `config/`, `package.json` and `.docs/` for `adyen`. Is the Adyen drop-in/web component integrated? Which components/pages? Is there an Adyen express/wallet component configured (Adyen supports Apple Pay/Google Pay through its drop-in)? Check `overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/payment.tsx` (it is modified on this branch) and any Adyen component dir. Report what payment methods are actually wired.

3. **Marketing opt-in / newsletter subscribe.** Grep `overrides/` for: `optin`, `opt-in`, `marketing`, `newsletter`, `subscribe`, `emailOptIn`, `receiveEmail`, `c_marketing`. Find:
   - where the opt-in checkbox is rendered (checkout? account create? footer subscribe?)
   - how the value is submitted / persisted (to SFCC customer or basket custom attribute?)
   - **whether the US-pre-checked-by-default exception is implemented at all** — grep for site-conditional default logic near the opt-in (look for siteId / SITE_ID / `us` comparisons). This is a house rule: unchecked everywhere except US where it's pre-checked. Report if it is implemented, partially implemented, or absent.
   - any Omneo / Emarsys sync code (grep `omneo`, `emarsys`).

4. **Checkout structure.** List the files under `overrides/app/pages/checkout/` and the base `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout/`. For the shipping step and payment step, state whether each is ALREADY OVERRIDDEN or BASE ONLY (needs copy-first), with base file line counts.

5. `.docs/` — find and read the Adyen integration doc (`.docs/integration/NN-adyen*.md` — numbered vendor docs) and anything about express checkout or marketing opt-in in `.docs/prd/`. Summarise what they say about Apple/Google Pay and about opt-in capture. Also grep `.docs/memory/` for express/applepay/adyen.

Be precise, evidence-led, absolute paths. Label clearly what is ABSENT vs present. Modify nothing.

input.description: Audit Global-E ownership for SFCC-950
input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (Salesforce PWA Kit v3 on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10; customisations in `overrides/`, base in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`, site config in `config/`).

I am auditing an effort estimate for SFCC-950: "VIP Rewards Redemption at Checkout via Global-E" — letting VIP/loyalty members redeem rewards during checkout on INTERNATIONAL sites, which route through Global-E rather than SFCC checkout.

The CRITICAL question: **how much of the international checkout front-end does Zimmermann actually control, versus what Global-E's hosted/own flow owns?** If Global-E owns the checkout UI entirely, a "FED - 3 days" figure may be mis-attributed (the work would be Global-E config/BED, not Zimmermann FED).

Investigate READ-ONLY (modify nothing). Report absolute paths + exact snippets:

1. **Global-E integration state.** Grep case-insensitively across `overrides/`, `config/`, `worker/`, `package.json`, and `.docs/` for: `global-e`, `globale`, `GlobalE`, `glbe`, `GLBE`, `borderfree`, `international checkout`. Report every real hit with path. State plainly: is Global-E integrated in the front-end at all, PARTIAL, or ABSENT (i.e. only mentioned in docs)?

2. **The checkout-ownership boundary.** This is the core deliverable. Determine and explain:
   - How does the app decide a shopper goes to Global-E vs SFCC checkout? Look for a redirect, a hand-off URL, a site-level flag. Check `overrides/app/pages/checkout-redirect/` (it exists and is modified on this branch) — read it fully and explain exactly what it does.
   - Is the Global-E checkout a full redirect to a Global-E-hosted domain, or an embedded/iframe/JS-overlay on Zimmermann's own domain? Quote the evidence.
   - Which of the 8 storefronts route which way? Read `config/sites.js` and `config/default.js` and any per-site config, and list site id -> checkout owner (SFCC vs Global-E) as best the config supports. The 8 sites are AU, US domestic, US intl, UK, EU domestic, EU intl, HK, ME.

3. **Loyalty / VIP / rewards.** Grep `overrides/`, `config/`, `.docs/` for: `vip`, `loyalty`, `rewards`, `omneo`, `points`, `tier`, `gold`, `vic`. Is there ANY loyalty UI or Omneo integration in the front-end today? Report what exists vs what is only documented. Note: Omneo is the loyalty platform on this project.

4. **`.docs/` deep read.** Find the numbered vendor integration docs (`.docs/integration/NN-*.md`) — locate and READ the Global-E one and the Omneo one (and any loyalty/VIP PRD in `.docs/prd/`). Summarise specifically:
   - what Global-E owns vs what Zimmermann owns in the checkout journey
   - anything about promotions/vouchers/rewards/discounts being passed to or supported by Global-E
   - any stated limitation on customising the Global-E checkout UI
   Quote the key lines.

5. Grep `.docs/memory/` and `.docs/prd/regional.md` for checkout ownership per site, and report what it says.

6. Grep the whole repo for `SFCC-950` and for any existing VIP/rewards ticket references.

Be precise, evidence-led, absolute paths, and clearly separate "implemented in code" from "described in docs only". Modify nothing.

############ 08-global-e.md ############
# 08 — Global-e (International Checkout)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Global-e is the international checkout owner for Zimmermann. When the shopper's destination is outside the domestic market of the active storefront, the PWA hands the cart to a Global-e-hosted checkout embedded as an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route.

PWA responsibilities:

- Reading target-currency prices from SFCC price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart
- Showing DDP/DDU duties messaging
- Assembling and triggering the cart handoff
- Embedding the Global-e checkout iframe
- Handling the order-completion return path

Server-side flows (nightly Global-e → SFCC price feed, daily SFCC → Global-e catalogue export, GiveX webhooks, and the post-order Global-e → SFCC webhook) are **outside** the PWA layer.

## 2. Checkout ownership matrix

| Storefront                                               | Destination                                                                                                | Checkout                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| AU (root)                                                | AU + Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands)                                                          | SFCC (REG-003). Avalara duties for NZ and New Caledonia; other Oceania is DDU. |
| US (`/us/`)                                              | US + Puerto Rico                                                                                           | SFCC (REG-005)                                                                 |
| US (`/en-ca/`, same SFCC site)                           | Canada, Mexico, all other Americas                                                                         | Global-e (REG-005, branched by shipping address)                               |
| UK (`/uk/`)                                              | UK only                                                                                                    | SFCC (REG-004)                                                                 |
| EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`) | EU domestic countries                                                                                      | SFCC (REG-006 dom)                                                             |
| EU international (`/en-ch/`)                             | Non-EU Europe + Africa + remainder                                                                         | Global-e (REG-006 intl)                                                        |
| HK (`/hk/`)                                              | HK + East, South, Southeast, and Central Asia (incl. China, Japan, India, Singapore) + Australia (REG-027) | Global-e (REG-007)                                                             |
| ME (`/en-ae/`)                                           | UAE + GCC + Levant + Egypt + Israel                                                                        | Global-e (REG-008)                                                             |

Checkout ownership branches at PDP and cart, not only at the checkout page.

> Non-Oceania shoppers who select "Australia" in the country selector are routed to the HK storefront (REG-027), not the geo-gated AU site.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
Shopper on a Global-e-served storefront (or chooses an international destination)
        │
        ▼
PDP / PLP / cart read the target-currency price from the SFCC Global-e-derived
price books (calculated by the nightly feed) and format it per locale
        │
        ▼
Add to cart — basket persists in SFCC in storefront currency
        │
        ▼
Checkout CTA — PWA calls SFCC to assemble the complete cart payload in the
shopper's target currency (per PRC-34..42)
        │
        ▼
SFCC posts the cart to Global-e (server-side) — "SendCart" — and returns a
`cartToken` representing the cloned cart on Global-e's side. SFCC also calls
`basket.reserveInventory()` before the SendCart request (default hold: 30 min).
        │
        ▼
PWA renders a Zimmermann checkout route that embeds the Global-e checkout
inside an iframe using the `cartToken`. The shopper remains on www.zimmermann.com
(parent frame); the iframe loads from Global-e's checkout origin.
        │
        ▼
Inside the iframe Global-e collects shipping address, payment, duties, and tax.
When the shopper clicks "Place Order", Global-e calls the SFCC
`Globale-ValidateCart` endpoint to check stock against SFCC inventory.
If stock is insufficient the shopper sees a popup and is redirected to cart —
no order is created on either side.
        │
        ▼
After validation passes, Global-e sends a `postMessage` to the parent frame.
The parent frame makes an AJAX request to SFCC `orderCreate()`, which converts
the basket to an SFCC order with status **Created**. If this call fails (session
expiry, stock change) Global-e's retry mechanism falls back to the
`SendOrderToMerchant` path to recreate and place the order.
        │
        ▼
Global-e calls SFCC's `SendOrderToMerchant` endpoint seconds later to enrich
the order with full international transaction data. Order status → **New**.
        │
        ▼
After fraud screening passes, Global-e calls SFCC's `PerformPayment` endpoint.
Payment status → **Paid**; export status → **Ready for Export**.
        │
        ▼
Order completion: the PWA navigates the parent frame to the Zimmermann
confirmation route, fetches the order from SFCC, and renders the confirmation.
The order number shown to shoppers is the Global-e order number
(format: `GE<digits><country>`, e.g. `GE111326998GB`); SFCC domestic orders
continue to show the SFCC order number.
```

- **Pre-checkout currency display.** Target-currency prices are read from the SFCC Global-e-derived price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart.
  SFCC holds these price books, regenerated nightly from Global-e's FX, coefficient, and rounding feed (PRC-34, PRC-38..40).
  Calculated prices are also in the SFCC search index so price filters and sort work on PLP and search results (PRC-41).
  The PWA does not convert prices client-side — it formats the SFCC-supplied target-currency price per locale (symbol position, decimal places including zero-decimal currencies, thousand separator) per PRC-47.
  HK and ME follow the same pattern: prices are read from HKD and AED SFCC price books, not from a Global-e client-side widget.
  No Global-e client-side script is needed to display pricing.

- **DDP/DDU duties messaging.** Shown on PDP per destination country, configurable per country (PRC-15). The data source for this flag (SFCC product attribute vs. Global-e price book field) is not specified in the PRDs — confirm with the integration team before implementing.

- **Handoff payload.** SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency at handoff — line items, quantities, target-currency prices, applied promotions, coupons, Retail Rewards, and gift cards (PRC-16).
  Global-e owns shipping, duties, and tax from the iframe onwards.

- **Iframe embed.** The Global-e checkout renders inside an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route. The `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` directive must list the Global-e checkout origin (see §9 item 1). Iframe height is managed via Global-e's `postMessage` contract.

- **Shipping country lock.** The shipping country is determined by the country selector pre-checkout and cannot be changed inside the Global-e iframe (REG-028).

- **Return path.** On order completion Global-e signals the parent frame via `postMessage`.
  The `postMessage` triggers an AJAX call from the parent frame to SFCC `orderCreate()` (see the flow diagram above for the full sequence).
  The PWA's `window` `"message"` event listener must enforce three conditions before acting on any message:
  1. **`event.origin`** matches the confirmed Global-e checkout origin (see §9 item 1).
  2. **`event.source`** equals the checkout `<iframe>` element's `contentWindow` — prevents other windows on the same trusted origin from triggering order completion.
  3. **Message schema** matches the expected Global-e payload shape — reject and ignore any message that does not conform.
  After all three checks pass:
  - Validate `orderRef` from the payload matches the expected Global-e format (`GE<digits><country>`, e.g. `GE111326998GB`) before using it. Reject and ignore the message if it does not match.
  - Construct the confirmation URL using `URLSearchParams` (or equivalent URL-safe encoding) rather than direct string interpolation — e.g. `new URLSearchParams({ orderRef }).toString()` — to prevent injection via a malformed payload value.
  - Navigate the parent frame to `/{prefix}/checkout/confirmation?<encoded-params>` and render the confirmation from the SFCC order record.
  The international order confirmation email is sent by Global-e; the PWA owns only the on-page confirmation display (CFD-071).

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Credential                         | Where used                                                     | Sensitivity                        |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Global-e Merchant ID               | Embedded in handoff request                                    | Public                             |
| Global-e API key and shared secret | Server-side only (SFCC → Global-e and Global-e webhook → SFCC) | Secret — never reaches the browser |

## 5. Data exchanged

**Browser / iframe → Global-e (client-side inputs):**

- Shopper IP and device user agent (passed by the browser)
- Pre-selected destination country (locked once inside the iframe)
- Order reference for return-webhook correlation

**SFCC → Global-e (SendCart server-side payload):**

- Cart line items (SKU, quantity, target-currency price)
- Guest email (via `globale.getGuestEmail` hook — pre-populates shopper email in the iframe)
- Saved addresses for logged-in shoppers (via `globale.getCustomerAddresses`)
- Didomi consent state mapped to Global-e's 0/1/2 scale (via `globale.getCookieConsent`)
- Marketing opt-in and direct communication consent flags (via `globale.getAllowMailsFromMerchant` / `globale.getAllowDirectCommunicationFromMerchant`)

**Global-e → Browser (return):** `postMessage` event to the parent frame triggering `orderCreate()`, after which the parent navigates to the Zimmermann confirmation route.

**Runtime session data available to the PWA:**

Global-e writes these SFCC session custom attributes on every storefront request after initialisation.
The PWA can read these from the SFCC session to determine country/currency context before handoff.

| Attribute         | Type    | Description                                  | Example |
| ----------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `geCountry`       | String  | Currently selected/detected country (ISO2)   | `GB`    |
| `geIsOperated`    | Boolean | Whether this country is operated by Global-e | `true`  |
| `geCurrency`      | String  | Currency ISO3 for the selected country       | `GBP`   |
| `gePriceStrategy` | String  | Pricing strategy (`DYNAMIC` or `FIXED`)      | `FIXED` |

Global-e also sets a `GlobalE_Data` cookie (available client-side) with four fields that map to session attributes:
`countryISO` → `geCountry`, `cultureCode` → `geCulture`, `currencyCode` → `geCurrency`, `apiVersion` → `geApiVersion`.
Note that `geCulture` and `geApiVersion` are session attributes written by Global-e but are not listed in the table above — they are only surfaced via the cookie.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- Pre-checkout prices come from standard SFCC product/price API responses. No extra Global-e network request sits on the PDP or PLP critical path.
- The handoff route embeds the Global-e iframe post-interaction; iframe load latency does not affect parent-page LCP.
- Emit `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Global-e checkout origin from the cart page to warm the TLS handshake before the iframe loads.
- Any retained Global-e client-side script (e.g. duties messaging) must be deferred and load after LCP.
- The Global-e team must configure `frame-ancestors` / `X-Frame-Options` to permit embedding under `www.zimmermann.com`.

## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure                                                                    | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SFCC Global-e-derived price book is missing or stale for a target currency | Show the storefront-currency price with the message "Final pricing in your currency shown at checkout." Do not silently fall back to an SFCC checkout for an international destination — that would route the order through the wrong checkout flow and carries tax / regulatory risk. |
| Handoff fails (Global-e API outage at cart → handoff)                      | Surface a hard error: "International checkout is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly." Do not place the order in SFCC.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Return webhook from Global-e to SFCC is delayed                            | Render the confirmation with the order reference and a "Your order is being processed" state. Full details render once SFCC receives the order.                                                                                                                                        |
| Cart total mismatch between SFCC and Global-e at handoff                   | Reject the order; surface a hard error. Never silently adjust totals.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## 8. Security

- The Global-e checkout domain is third-party. Cross-site cookies do not propagate — cart context is passed inside the handoff payload, not via cookies.
- The `postMessage` listener in the parent frame must enforce all three checks documented in §3 — `event.origin`, `event.source`, and message schema — plus `orderRef` format validation and URL-safe query encoding before constructing the confirmation URL. See §3 "Return path" for the full requirements.

## 9. Open items

1. **Iframe embedding requirements.** Global-e to confirm and supply:

   - The `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` value for production and non-production Global-e checkout origins — needed to configure the storefront's security headers.
   - The `postMessage` trusted sender origin — the vendor guide confirms that the Global-e iframe sends a `postMessage` to the parent frame to trigger `orderCreate()`, but does not specify the exact origin string or the full message schema. The `event.origin` value and message payload shape must be obtained from Global-e directly before the listener can be safely implemented.
     Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.

2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order (from SFCC), to decide between full order detail and a "View on tracking page" fallback.
   Full detail needs: line items, totals in both shopper and base currency, shipping address, and fulfilment status.

Omneo is the system of record for customer identity, loyalty, and clienteling; SFCC syncs bidirectionally via MuleSoft webhooks (CFD-012). Customer authentication uses SFCC Configurable account management; passwords are not migrated from Magento, so all existing customers must reset at go-live (CFD-013).
121:- Free shipping thresholds configurable in Business Manager **independently per delivery method and per storefront** (e.g. Ground free above $1000, Express free above $2000) (OM-010). Eligible VIC groups get free shipping regardless of order value (CFD-051)

174:- Address mismatch: error/warning before order completion. Express payment methods (Apple Pay Express, Google Pay Express) are rejected at Adyen level if the address doesn't match the storefront region. The system will not offer ship-to countries outside the storefront region (PAY-015)

############ 07-adyen.md — express / wallet ############
7:The PWA loads the Adyen Web Drop-in at the payment step of checkout. Card details are tokenised inside an Adyen-hosted iframe — they never reach Zimmermann or SFCC infrastructure.
11:- Adyen Web Drop-in initialisation, configuration, and rendering
14:- Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Klarna where supported (launch and August 2026 wave)
23:- **Payment methods in scope:** Web Drop-in, 3DS2, RevenueProtect, Tokenisation, Pay by Link, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna where applicable.
24:- **Adyen Web SDK version:** Adyen Web v6 (current stable major) at implementation start, pinned in the bundle, upgraded on a quarterly cadence. v6 instantiates the Drop-in via an async constructor (`const checkout = await AdyenCheckout({...})`) — the v5-era `AdyenCheckout.create()` factory was removed in v6 — requires Adyen Checkout API v69 or later, makes `countryCode` a required initialisation property per the v5→v6 migration guide (the Sessions flow supplies it automatically from the session payload), and uses CSS custom properties for styling.

46:and as a native button for Apple Pay / Google Pay
49:User submits — Drop-in handles tokenisation, 3DS2 inline, and the redirect
53:Drop-in calls the merchant return URL on success → SFCC reconciles → PWA
57:- The Adyen Sessions flow is used. One server-side `/sessions` call from SFCC creates a payment session; the Drop-in handles everything thereafter — including 3DS2 inline rendering, PayPal / Klarna redirects, and final result reporting — without further `/payments` calls from the PWA.
61:- The Drop-in for cards renders inside an Adyen-hosted iframe, so the PWA bundle never touches PAN, CVV, or cardholder name.
62:- When paying with a previously saved card, the PWA requires the customer to re-enter the card's CVV/CVC at the point of payment (PAY-022). The CVV/CVC field is captured inside the Adyen Drop-in's stored-card flow; the value lives in React state only, is never logged or persisted client-side, and is cleared on submit/unmount — see §8. The 3DS re-challenge decision is owned by Adyen (outside the PWA boundary); the PWA does not control whether 3DS re-prompts.
83:The Adyen client key is public and embedded in the Drop-in init. It is bound to an Adyen API credential (web-service user) that is origin-restricted per environment in the Adyen Customer Area. All server-side credentials (API key, HMAC secret) live in the SFCC cartridge — the PWA never holds or sees them.

91:| Adyen → Drop-in → PWA | Tokenised payment method blob; 3DS challenge data; final result code | The blob is opaque to the PWA and is forwarded verbatim to SFCC |

- **HS codes and tax engine for Oceania (PAY-066, PAY-067):** Correct for Oceania today; transition to Global-e not yet confirmed.
- **Order Management open items** (OM-002 export gating, OM-017/018 NewStore status taxonomy, OM-034 back-in-stock FIFO logic) live in [orderManagement.md §6](./orderManagement.md).

## 17. Explicit Non-Goals (at launch)

- Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna (August 2026)
- Social login implementation (confirmed in scope, but implementation Open)
- Checkout A/B testing logic
- Custom per-market UI variations beyond what is specified

- PayPal via Adyen with redirect and return; billing address pre-populated from PayPal callback (PAY-003, PAY-023)

- Retail Rewards (AP21 VIP balance) — see section 12

### Targeting August 2026 (confirmed in scope, not launch)

- Available methods presented at the payment step, configured per storefront in Business Manager (PAY-001)

# SFCC-804 Audit — Marketing Opt-In for Apple Pay / Google Pay Express Checkout

**Repo state at audit:** branch `feature/SFCC-11_cart`, with unresolved merge conflicts (`UU`) in `.claude/registry/*` and a few `ui-kits` files. `overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/payment.tsx` is `M` (staged modified); `checkout-header.tsx` is untracked (`??`).

---

## HEADLINE ANSWER

**Apple Pay / Google Pay express checkout is ABSENT as a working flow.** What exists is: (a) two **non-functional, click-handler-less** wallet buttons in the cart drawer, and (b) an **inherited, config-disabled** Salesforce Payments express path from the base template that is wired into PDP but cannot activate because `sfPayments.enabled = false`.

SFCC-804 as written has **no host flow to attach to**. This is a genuine sequencing finding.

---

## 1. Express payments / wallet buttons

### (a) Zimmermann implementation in `overrides/` — DEAD BUTTONS

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx`

The Apple Pay and Google Pay buttons render but **have no `onClick`**. This is the entire wallet-button JSX:

```tsx
{!isInternational && (
  <>
    <ZimmButton
      variant="secondary"
      label={intl.formatMessage(messages.applePay)}
      fullWidth
      hideLabelVisually
      iconLeading={<PayMarkSlot><ApplePayMark /></PayMarkSlot>}
    />
    <ZimmButton
      variant="secondary"
      label={intl.formatMessage(messages.googlePay)}
      fullWidth
      hideLabelVisually
      iconLeading={<PayMarkSlot><GooglePayMark /></PayMarkSlot>}
    />
  </>
)}
```

Only the **Checkout** button above them has behaviour (`handleCheckoutClick`). The component's own decision log states this explicitly at line 273:

```
// 4. useExpressCheckoutEnabled() checked (per plan.md step 5.1's own instruction) but not wired
//    into this component: it gates a *different* axis (device/browser eligibility, SFCC-309, not
//    yet scoped ...). Wiring it in would be scope this step wasn't asked to add.
```

These are Figma-fidelity chrome only. Supporting assets exist (`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/assets/svg/apple-pay-logo.svg`, `google-pay-logo.svg`) but are inlined as SVG paths, not wired to any payment SDK.

Mounted via `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx:26` → `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useCartDrawer.ts:6`. **New on this branch** — not present on `origin/develop`.

### (b) Base SFCC template code — PRESENT but CONFIG-DISABLED

The base package ships a complete Salesforce Payments express suite:

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/sf-payments-express-buttons/index.jsx` (1051 lines)
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/sf-payments-express/index.jsx` (70 lines)
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-sf-payments.js`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/sf-payments-utils.js` (`applepay` / `googlepay` button-style maps at lines 477-484)

Zimmermann's PDP **does** consume this path — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`:

```tsx
// line 57
import { useSFPayments, useExpressCheckoutEnabled } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-sf-payments';
// line 91
import SFPaymentsExpressButtons from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/sf-payments-express-buttons';
// line 578
const { pdp: showExpressOnPDP } = useExpressCheckoutEnabled();
// line 967
if (showExpressOnPDP && !isProductASet && !isProductPartOfBundle && activeCurrency && priceData.currentPrice) {
  buttons.push(<SFPaymentsExpressButtons key="express-buttons" usage={EXPRESS_BUY_NOW} ... />);
}
```

**It is hard-off.** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/config/default.js:186-190`:

```js
sfPayments: {
  enabled: false,
  sdkUrl: '',
  metadataUrl: '',
},
```

And `use-sf-payments.js:109-114`:

```js
export const useSFPaymentsEnabled = () => {
    const config = getConfig()
    const localEnabled = config?.app?.sfPayments?.enabled ?? true
    const apiEnabled = useShopperConfiguration('SalesforcePaymentsAllowed') === true
    return localEnabled && apiEnabled
}
```

`useExpressCheckoutEnabled()` therefore returns `{pdp: false, miniCart: false, cart: false, checkout: false}` on every site. `SFPaymentsExpressButtons` never renders. No override of `config/default.js`'s `sfPayments` block exists in any env file (`config/dev.js`, `sit.js`, `staging.js`, `uat.js`, `production.js` — checked, zero hits).

**Architectural note:** Salesforce Payments is *not* Zimmermann's payment stack — Adyen is (see §2). The `sf-payments-*` path is inherited base code on a road Zimmermann isn't taking. Base `checkout/index.jsx:218` branches `sfPaymentsEnabled ? <SFPaymentsSheet/> : <Payment/>` — Zimmermann lands on the `<Payment/>` branch, which is the Adyen override.

### (c) Incidental / infrastructure-only matches

```

138:      'applepay.cdn-apple.com', // Apple Pay SDK loaded by Adyen Drop-in
```

Everything else matching `express` in `overrides/` is Express.js (the Node server), not express checkout.

### VERDICT §1

| Surface | Status |
|---|---|
| Cart drawer wallet buttons (Zimmermann) | **PRESENT BUT NON-FUNCTIONAL** — no `onClick`, no SDK, no basket/payment call |
| PDP express buttons (base `SFPaymentsExpressButtons`) | **WIRED BUT DISABLED** — `sfPayments.enabled: false`, unreachable |
| Checkout-page express strip (base) | **DISABLED** — same gate; and Zimmermann uses the Adyen `<Payment/>` branch instead |
| Adyen wallet components | **ABSENT** — no Apple Pay / Google Pay configuration in the Adyen integration |
| **Overall express-checkout wallet flow** | **ABSENT** |

---

## 2. Adyen

**Integrated and real — but cards/redirect methods only, no wallet configuration.**

`package.json`:
```
127:    "@adyen/adyen-salesforce-pwa": "^4.5.0",
128:    "@adyen/adyen-web": "^6.44.0",
117:      "path": "build/adyen.js",     (separate bundle entry)
```

Files touching Adyen:
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/payment.tsx` — the Drop-in host (238 lines)
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/ssr.js:23,197,219` — `registerAdyenEndpoints(app, runtime)` + `/api/adyen/payment/cancel`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/ssr/paymentMetadata.ts` — `GET /api/payment-metadata`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts` — Adyen CSP hosts
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/static/adyen.css`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/checkout-redirect/index.tsx`, `/overrides/app/pages/confirmation/index.tsx`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts:188-189` — `declare module '@adyen/adyen-salesforce-pwa';` (ships no types)

**What `payment.tsx` actually renders** — a single generic `<AdyenCheckout>` with **no `paymentMethodsConfiguration`, no `applepay`/`googlepay` block, no merchant identifier**:

```tsx
<AdyenCheckout
    authToken={authToken}
    customerId={customerId}
    site={site}
    locale={adyenLocale}
    navigate={navigate}
    basket={basket}
    orderNo={orderNo}
    onError={[...]}
/>
```

The only wallet reference in the whole file is a defensive comment in the error handler:
```
// SCRIPT_ERROR — a payment method's JS SDK failed to load (e.g. Apple Pay
//   blocked by CSP); the dropin removes that method, others still work.
```

Method availability comes from the SFCC-side Adyen session payload, not the storefront. Methods referenced in comments as actually exercised: **card, Klarna, PayPal, 3DS**. Notably, the file's bulk of logic is billing-address sync (`updateBillingAddressForBasket`), a 409-avoidance promise queue, and an error boundary — i.e. **the standard payment-step Drop-in**, not an express flow.

**Critically for SFCC-804: Adyen only mounts at the checkout payment step, after shipping.** `payment.tsx` gates render on `billingReadyKey === currentBillingKey && currentBillingKey !== null`, which requires `basket.shipments[0].shippingAddress` to exist. entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

content.text:
Evidence gathering complete. Confluence was unreachable this session (repeated connection drops on page 385318913 and search), so the table figures are taken as given from the brief and everything below is corroborated from Jira, the codebase, and `.docs/`.

---

# FED Estimate Audit — SFCC-866 / SFCC-804 / SFCC-950

**Cross-cutting finding first: all three tickets have `customfield_10231` = `null`. Zero acceptance criteria across all three.** The table commits 7 FED days against three stories with no testable criteria. All three sit under epic SFCC-24 "Enhancements", all To Do.

---

## 1. SFCC-866 — Auto-remove cart item when moving to wishlist if already in wishlist

**What it actually asks for:** when a shopper moves a cart item to wishlist and it's already there, remove it from the cart anyway instead of leaving it and showing an error.

**AC quality: NO — 0 ACs.** Description is one narrative paragraph. No comments, no issue links.

**What exists already — the whole flow is built and already overridden:**
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/index.tsx` (146 lines) — the exact branch point. `await onRemove()` sits **only** inside the `'success'` branch; the `'already-in-wishlist'` branch fires a toast and returns.
- `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (817 lines) — membership test is a synchronous in-memory `.some()` over `wishlist.customerProductListItems`, short-circuiting before any network call. **No new fetch needed.**
- `overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts`, `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` (421 lines), `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/`
- **Zero copy-first on the drawer surface.** Every file is already `.tsx` under `overrides/`.
- Not overridden: the `/cart` **page** route, still base (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx`, 1515 lines).

**FED work breakdown (drawer-only, after SFCC-272 lands):**

| Item | Days |
|---|---|
| Move `await onRemove()` into the already-in-wishlist branch | 0.1 |
| Decide + apply feedback treatment (reword toast, or delete the `alreadyInWishlistItemIds` state machine + `onAlreadyInWishlist` prop chain) | 0.25 |
| Contentful `cart.item.alreadyInWishlist` uiCopy key change/retire | 0.15 |
| Tests — invert assertions across `zimmCartItemActions/index.test.tsx`, `cartDrawerContainer.test.tsx`, `useCartMessages.test.tsx` | 0.3 |
| Story + 3 docblocks that cite SFCC-272 AC6 | 0.15 |
| Verify basket/wishlist cache consistency on the new path | 0.15 |
| Cross-site smoke (behaviour is site-agnostic — auth-only, no Global-E/locale branching) | 0.2 |
| PR + CodeRabbit + rework | 0.25 |

**Bottom-up FED total: ~1.5 days**

**Verdict vs table (FED 2): OVER by ~0.5 day.** Biggest single reason: priced as if move-to-wishlist had to be built or copy-first'd; it's already built and already overridden, and the functional change is one line moved.

**The more useful number: ~0.25 day if folded into SFCC-272 now.** SFCC-272 ("Cart Item - Remove and Wishlist Actions") is **In Progress** on this very branch. As a separate later ticket you pay ~1.5 days purely to re-open, reverse and re-test work being written this sprint.

**Dependency on unbuilt work:** Soft yes — SFCC-272 is In Progress, not done. Scope risk: SFCC-866 is labelled **CAI-008**, which in `.docs/prd/cart.md:23` is the **cart page**, but the built surface is the drawer. If `/cart` is in scope, add 1.5–2.5 days for the 1515-line copy-first — though that cost properly belongs to the cart-page story.

**Blockers/unknowns:**
- **Directly contradicts SFCC-272 AC6**, which is cited in code, test names and a story in 4 places (e.g. `useCartMessages.ts:63` — *"the caller leaves the cart line untouched"*). AC6 needs formally superseding, not silently overwriting.
- **Wishlist hosting (SFCC vs Omneo) is NOT confirmed** — ENH-038/039, both "Under Review" (`.docs/prd/cart.md:145`, projectState.md). If it moves to Omneo, the membership check is rewritten.
- Jira note "Double check if in designs (Kiera Rikard-Bell)" is unresolved.

**Questions, and who:**
1. **Emma Kirwan / Kiera Rikard-Bell** — does the "already in wishlist" feedback survive (reworded, e.g. "already in Wishlist — removed from bag") or disappear? Copy needed either way; the key is Contentful-sourced.
2. **Tim Lavelle / Squad A** — fold into SFCC-272 before it ships rather than build AC6 then reverse it?
3. **BA/PO** — drawer only, or the `/cart` page too (the CAI-008 label implies the page)?
4. **PO** — formally supersede SFCC-272 AC6.

---

## 2. SFCC-804 — Marketing opt-in capture for Apple Pay / Google Pay express

**What it actually asks for:** capture marketing consent from shoppers using express wallets, who never see the opt-in checkbox.

**AC quality: NO — 0 ACs, and the ticket says so itself:** *"This story is currently a placeholder — no solution has been agreed... Requires input from Emma/Rebecca (business), Keira (UX), and Tim (technical feasibility) before ACs can be written."*

**What exists already:**
- **Apple/Google Pay express: ABSENT.** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx` renders both wallet buttons with **no `onClick`** — `grep -n onClick` returns exactly one hit (line 209, the plain Checkout button). Figma chrome only.
- Base Salesforce Payments express suite exists but is **hard-off**: `config/default.js:186-190` → `sfPayments: {enabled: false}`, with no env override. Wrong stack anyway — Zimmermann is Adyen.
- **Adyen is payment-step only:** `overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/payment.tsx` (238 lines) mounts a generic `<AdyenCheckout>` with no `paymentMethodsConfiguration`, no applepay/googlepay block, and gates render on a shipping address existing.
- **Marketing opt-in checkbox: ABSENT entirely**, at both PRD-mandated touchpoints. No `c_marketing`/`emailOptIn`/`acceptsMarketing` anywhere in `overrides/`.
- **US pre-check (REG-057 / CFD-009): ABSENT**, and no site-conditional consent helper exists to copy.
- No `overrides/app/pages/account|login|registration`. Omneo/Emarsys "Not started".
- Checkout shell `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout/index.jsx` (356 lines): **BASE ONLY**, copy-first required to insert anything between shipping and payment.

**Technical constraint I'd flag (my analysis, not from a doc):** you cannot render a consent checkbox *inside* the Apple Pay or Google Pay payment sheet — that UI is vendor-controlled. So the only viable touchpoints are before the button is pressed, or post-purchase.

**FED work breakdown — conditional, because no solution exists:**

*Scenario A — opt-in already sits on the cart above the express buttons:* **0 days.** SFCC-383/384 are titled *"(Cart Page & Mini Bag)"* — the same surface SFCC-325 targets. If the checkbox renders there, an express shopper does see it. The genuinely uncovered gap is PDP express buy-now only.

*Scenario B — post-purchase capture on the confirmation page (most likely real solution):*

| Item | Days |
|---|---|
| Opt-in component (checkbox + consent copy) + story + test | 0.5 |
| Detect express-checkout order on confirmation; conditional render | 0.5 |
| Persist — new SFCC custom attribute (none exists) + error/retry | 0.75 |
| US pre-check site-conditional helper — first of its kind, 8 sites | 0.5 |
| Didomi gating + fail-closed on unknown consent | 0.25 |
| 8 storefronts / 11 locales verification + translations | 0.5 |
| PR + CodeRabbit + rework | 0.25 |

**Bottom-up FED total: 0 days (A) or ~3.25 days (B).**

**Verdict vs table (FED 2): NOT ESTIMABLE AS WRITTEN.** Against the likely real solution, **UNDER by ~1.25 days**; against scenario A, **OVER by 2**. Biggest single reason: a number was placed on a story that states it has no agreed solution — it's a placeholder figure on a placeholder story, not a sized estimate.

**Dependency on unbuilt work: YES — explicitly. This presumes a feature that does not exist.** Four deep:
1. **SFCC-383** (Apple Pay Express Button, Cart Page & Mini Bag) — **To Do, unassigned**; **SFCC-384** (Google Pay Express) — **To Do**. Wallets are an **explicit launch non-goal** (`.docs/prd/checkout.md:277`, §17), targeting **August 2026**, and blocked on client-owned Apple/Google merchant IDs (`.docs/integration/07-adyen.md` §10 item 1).
2. **SFCC-325** — **To Do**, and note it is actually titled *"Cart Page – **Newsletter Sign Up Component**"*, not "Marketing Opt-In Checkbox" as SFCC-804's description claims. Possibly a different thing.
3. The base opt-in checkbox (CFD-009 / REG-057 / CRM-195) — never built once.
4. Omneo/Emarsys — Not started; CRM-198 carries an unresolved legal conflict on *when* a guest record may be created, which is precisely what this story raises.

**Blockers/unknowns:**
- No agreed solution, by the ticket's own words.
- The note *"Under shipping and on top of payments"* describes the **standard checkout page** — which an express shopper by definition never sees. It likely describes CFD-009, not this story.
- `.docs/prd/regional.md:146` logs REG-057/058 opt-in touchpoints as an open Unresolved Dependency.
- GDPR/legal sign-off flagged in the ticket itself.

**Questions, and who:**
1. **Emma Kirwan / Rebecca Jourdan** — if the opt-in sits on the cart drawer alongside the express buttons, is this story needed at all? Is the real gap just PDP express buy-now?
2. **Keira Rikard-Bell** — design for the chosen touchpoint; none exists.
3. **Tim Lavelle** — confirm the wallet sheets can't host the checkbox, and that post-purchase is the fallback.
4. **Rebecca / legal** — is post-purchase consent capture GDPR-acceptable?
5. **BA/PM** — SFCC-325 is "Newsletter Sign Up Component", not an opt-in checkbox. Which is actually the dependency?
6. **Delivery lead** — should this be estimated at all before wallets exist (Aug 2026 wave, explicit launch non-goal)?

---

## 3. SFCC-950 — VIP Rewards redemption at checkout via Global-E

**What it actually asks for:** let VIP members redeem rewards during international (Global-E) checkout; currently domestic-only.

**AC quality: NO — 0 ACs.** Worse, the description isn't a Zimmermann requirement — it is **Global-E's own reply pasted in** (*"pass the points and value from the Magento cart to **our** checkout"*), referencing **Magento** (the platform being replaced) and **AP21**. Pre-replatform vendor commentary.

**What exists already:**
- **Global-E front-end: ABSENT.** Only config metadata in `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` (`checkoutOwner: 'sfcc' | 'global-e' | 'hybrid'`) plus a literal no-op stub in `zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx`:
  `export const navigateInternationalCheckoutStub = (navigate) => { navigate('/checkout'); }` — commented *"TODO(SFCC-880, SFCC-63)"* and *"Global-e: 'Not started'"*.
- No `cartToken`, no SendCart, no iframe, no `postMessage` listener. (`overrides/app/pages/checkout-redirect/` is **Adyen**, not Global-E.)
- **Loyalty/VIP UI: ABSENT.** No account pages at all. `.docs/integration/04-omneo.md` §1 puts *"loyalty reads and writes"* explicitly **out of PWA scope** (server-side).
- Ownership (`08-global-e.md` §2 + `countries.ts`): Global-E = HK, ME, en-ch, en-ca. SFCC = AU, UK, EU domestic. US = hybrid.

**The mis-attribution, with evidence:**
- `.docs/integration/08-global-e.md` §3: the Global-E checkout renders **inside an iframe**, and *"Global-e owns shipping, duties, and tax from the iframe onwards."* A redemption UI *at checkout* therefore lives inside **Global-E's product**, not Zimmermann's front-end.
- Same §3: *"**SFCC posts the cart to Global-e (server-side)** — 'SendCart'"*. Passing points/value is a server-side payload change = **BED / SFCC cartridge**, not FED.
- PRC-16 already specifies the handoff payload as carrying *"applied promotions, coupons, **Retail Rewards**, and gift cards"* — the plumbing is server-side and already spec'd.

**FED work breakdown:**

| Item | Days |
|---|---|
| Redemption UI inside the Global-E checkout | **0 — Global-E vendor scope** |
| Pass points/value SFCC → Global-E (SendCart) | **0 — BED / SFCC cartridge** |
| Pre-handoff reward balance / applied-state display in cart (only if agreed; needs a loyalty data source that doesn't exist client-side) | 1.5 |
| Confirmation-page display of a redeemed reward | 0.5 |

**Bottom-up FED total: 0 days as literally scoped; ≤2 days if a pre-handoff cart display is added.**

**Verdict vs table (FED 3): MIS-ATTRIBUTED — delta −3 to −1 days.** Biggest single reason: the deliverable sits inside a vendor-hosted iframe Zimmermann does not control, and the data change is server-side. (BED 1 day also looks low for a SendCart payload extension plus AP21 reconciliation.)

**Dependency on unbuilt work: YES, severely.** The entire Global-E checkout front-end — iframe route, cartToken handoff, postMessage return path, CSP `frame-src` — is unbuilt, currently a one-line `navigate('/checkout')` stub (SFCC-63 / SFCC-880, both open). And `08-global-e.md` §9 open item 1: Global-E has not supplied the frame-src origin or the postMessage schema — *"Neither can be guessed."*

**Blockers/unknowns — this ticket contradicts a signed-off requirement:**
1. **PAY-039 (signed off) says the opposite:** *"HK, ME, EU International: Retail Rewards **cannot** be redeemed online.
